description: Confirm and pin DELETE /api/pitches/{id} semantics, and make its cascade complete. Admin-only (assessor and viewer 403), 200 on success, 404 on unknown id. Deleting a pitch must remove every dependent record in the same transaction — stage history, contact links, file links, assessments, meetings, and the meeting attendee rows hanging off those meetings — leaving no dangling references. Contacts, organisations and users referenced by the pitch must survive. Attendee rows are currently de-associated rather than deleted (meeting_attendees.meeting_id is NOT NULL), which makes deleting a pitch that has a meeting with attendees fail; fix it at the ORM relationship level so it holds on both SQLite and Postgres rather than relying on a DB cascade.
expectedBehavior: admin DELETE returns 200 and a subsequent GET of the pitch returns 404
assessor DELETE -> 403; viewer DELETE -> 403; unauthenticated -> 401 or 403
Deleting an unknown pitch id returns 404
Deleting a pitch with a meeting that has attendees returns 200 and removes both the meeting and its attendee rows
After a delete, no pitch_stage_history, pitch_contacts, pitch_file_links, assessments, meetings or meeting_attendees rows remain for that pitch
Contacts, organisations and users linked to the deleted pitch remain retrievable
Deleting a meeting that has attendees also removes its attendee rows
verificationSteps: cd backend && pytest tests/test_pitches.py -k 'delete or cascade or rbac'

description: Add a delete affordance to PitchDetailPage. A 'Delete' button sits in the page header action row alongside Edit / Log Meeting / New Assessment, styled as a red-outlined warning, and is shown only to admins (assessors and viewers see nothing). Clicking it opens a confirmation dialog that names the pitch, reports how many assessments and meetings will be destroyed with it (reusing the counts the page has already loaded), warns that the action cannot be undone, and requires the user to type the pitch's exact title before the confirm control becomes enabled. Confirming calls api.delete('/pitches/{id}') and navigates to /pitches on success. Cancel, Escape and an outside click all dismiss without calling the API. A failed delete keeps the dialog open and shows the server's error message inline.
expectedBehavior: The Delete control is shown for admin and hidden for assessor and viewer
Opening the dialog makes no API call; the dialog names the pitch and shows its assessment and meeting counts
The confirm control is disabled until the typed text exactly matches the pitch title, and a partial or wrong title never calls api.delete
Confirming calls api.delete('/pitches/{id}') once and then navigates to /pitches
Cancel, Escape and an outside click close the dialog without calling api.delete
A rejected api.delete shows the error message, keeps the dialog open and does not navigate
